## You cannot pin behaviour when the behaviour is wrong

- Standard refactoring playbook: characterise old behaviour, then change freely
- Here the old behaviour was **incorrect**, so the fixes deliberately move the numbers
  away from the 2014 published results
- So there is no golden output. **What do you verify against?**

## Three oracles

| Type | Script | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Differential | `parity_orthopen.R` | vs validated orthopen v1.1.0: $\max\lvert B_{ref}-B_{new}\rvert = 0$ on 5 deterministic cases; the seeded disjoint case agrees to $<10^{-6}$ |
| Metamorphic | `old_vs_fixed_logistic.R` | label-flip antisymmetry restored: ~0.62 → 0.000 |
| Pseudo-oracle | `simulation_recovery.R` | survival path vs ground truth: support-recovery AUC ~0.66 vs ~0.50 null, 10/10 seeds |

. . .

The survival path is exactly where differential testing **cannot** reach.

::: notes
Longest beat; the taxonomy is the transferable content. Slow down.
Verified against validation/README.md and parity_orthopen.R: five exact cases plus one
RNG-seeded disjoint case checked to <1e-6, so do NOT say "bit-for-bit on six cases".
:::

## REG-01: plausible, idiomatic, wrong

Labels in $\{-1,+1\}$, but the gradient used the $\{0,1\}$ cross-entropy form:

$$\color{#B2182B}{-\,(Y - \sigma(Xw))}$$

$$\color{#1B7837}{-\,X^{\top}\!\left(\frac{y}{1+\exp(y\,Xw)}\right)\Big/ m}$$

- Inherited from the 2014 research code
- The buggy version violates label-flip symmetry; the fix restores it **and lowers held-out logistic loss**
- Written by a human. The failure mode is not new; cheap verification is.

::: notes
The old draft quoted a 7.1% held-out loss reduction. I could not find that figure in the
orthoMTL repo, so it is deliberately NOT on the slide. Re-run validation/old_vs_fixed_logistic.R
(needs the legacy source via ORTHOPEN_LEGACY) and add the number here only if it reproduces.
:::

## Would a skill file have saved the round-trips?

**The tell.** Two CRAN rejections, both human review: an invalid `+ file LICENSE` field, then a
hard-coded `set.seed()`. And `.claude/settings.local.json` almost shipped in the tarball.

. . .

**The test.** Seed the package with CRAN defects; give an agent the CRAN task under one of
**six conditions** (no skill, three public skills, a hindsight skill, raw handbook text):

- Frozen prompt, fresh tree per run, blocks interleaved, outputs **blinded**
- Machine checks + a judge **calibrated on mutants first** (92 % detection, 8 % false positives)
- `r n_runs` completed runs, `r n_arm` per arm

::: notes
Everything is pre-registered; the SHA-256 of the blind map was committed before scoring.
n went 5 to 10 per arm after an interim look: say so on the limitations slide, not here.
:::

## Result: machine checks saturate, the judge barely moves

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.3
dotplot("judge_nc", "Judge-flagged non-compliant criteria per tree", integer = TRUE)
```

- **`r n_seed`/`r n_runs`** completed runs fixed all four seeded machine-detectable defects, **the no-skill control included**, with no regressions
- Judge flags come from **two** criteria; no arm separates from the control, not even the hindsight arm A4

::: notes
Lead with the uncomfortable part: the hindsight arm (written from this package's own failures)
does not beat the no-skill control. The control did well because it runs R CMD check
against itself. That is the slide-8 point, measured.
:::

## What this cannot tell you

- **Every arm, A0 included, could read an offline copy of the CRAN docs.** The honest claim is
  "no benefit beyond documentation already at hand", not "skills are useless"
- n = 1 package, 1 agent, 1 model version
- **n was extended 5 → 10 per arm after an interim unblinded look** (post-hoc, not pre-registered)
- 3 runs lost to API rate limits, excluded (`r n_runs` of 60 analysed)
- No positive control showed the instrument *could* detect a gain; descriptive only, no significance testing

## What transfers

- **Behavioural oracles** → semantic correctness. Domain knowledge decides which
  metamorphic relation is the right one; the agent cannot supply that.
- **Conformance oracles** → compliance correctness. `R CMD check` is a machine oracle the
  agent runs against itself. **That is why it scales, and why a skill file added nothing on top.**
- Slop is what happens when generation gets cheap and verification does not.

<br>

## Backup: what I would change next time

- Seed **judge-only** defects so the judge has live criteria
- Add a deliberately handicapped arm as a positive control
- Multi-rep judging; judge set without unrepairable constants (maintainer email)
- More packages, more models
